title: Raw Identifiers with Backticks
hints: Backticked names are ordinary identifiers once declared.
Interpolating an enum case prints its (backticked) name without backticks.
The first line prints the raw value of `` `2` `` and the case name of `` `1.1` ``.
jsBridge: Swift 6.2 raw identifiers allow almost any text in backticks as a name, like `` func `test adding two items`() ``. JS allows only computed property names (`obj['any text']`).

compass.q: JS test names are strings (`it('adds two items')`). How does Swift Testing use raw identifiers to get the same readability?
Can you name an enum case `` `1st` ``? Why was that previously impossible?
Raw identifiers vs the `@Test("display name")` argument: which would you use?
Would you allow raw identifiers outside tests? Where could they hurt?
